pll2d11c2-d1e3514.summary: Asks whether the good angels advance in merit or reward until judgment.

pll2d11c2-d1e3517.summary: Reports some who think they advance in merit daily, serving our benefit, and in reward, in knowledge and love of God; though they received perfect beatitude at confirmation, it grows as they love and know more, and their charity is both merit and reward.
claims: One view: angels grow in merit and beatitude.
Their charity is both merit and reward.

pll2d11c2-d1e3533.summary: Says they confirm by the saints' testimonies that angels advance in knowledge and so in beatitude.

pll2d11c2-d1e3537.summary: Cites Isa 63:1 ('who is this who comes from Edom?') and Ps 23:8 ('who is this king of glory?') as angels marveling at the ascending Christ, showing they knew the mystery of the Word incarnate more fully after its fulfillment, and so advance in knowledge of the Godhead.
claims: Angels knew the Incarnation more fully after its fulfillment.

pll2d11c2-d1e3571.summary: Cites Eph 3:9–10, the hidden mystery made known to principalities and powers through the Church, and Jerome: the angels did not fully understand it until Christ's passion was complete and the apostles' preaching spread.
claims: Angels did not fully understand the mystery before the passion (Jerome).

pll2d11c2-d1e3591.summary: Notes that Augustine seems to contradict this: the mystery was not hidden from the angels but known to them from the ages.

pll2d11c2-d1e3608.summary: Notes that the illustrious doctors seem to disagree.

pll2d11c2-d1e3611.summary: Resolves following Haymo: the higher angels, as intimates and messengers, knew it in part from the ages; the lower did not until fulfilled and preached, when all knew it perfectly.
claims: Higher angels knew the mystery partially; lower angels learned it later.

pll2d11c2-d1e3626.summary: Concludes that all angels advanced in knowledge of divine mysteries over time, and so these say angelic knowledge and beatitude increase until the final consummation, when they will neither increase nor decrease.
claims: Angelic knowledge and beatitude grow until the consummation.

pll2d11c2-d1e3632.summary: Reports the other view: at confirmation the angels received such love and knowledge of the Godhead that they do not advance in them; they grew in knowledge of external things, like the Incarnation, but not in contemplating the Trinity, nor in charity, nor in merit as to its power, though in number of merits.
claims: Another view: angels did not grow in contemplation or charity after confirmation.

pll2d11c2-d1e3635.summary: Judges the first view more probable: angels advance in knowledge and other things until judgment.
claims: Lombard prefers the view that angels progress until judgment.

pll2d11c2-d1e3638.summary: Notes that some authorities seem to oppose this.

pll2d11c2-d1e3641.summary: Cites Isidore: angels know all things in the Word before they happen; but he did not say all angels know all perfectly, so he did not exclude their progress.
claims: Isidore does not exclude angelic progress.

pll2d11c2-d1e3660.summary: Cites Gregory: what do they not know there where they know the one who knows all? This is to be understood of things whose knowledge beatifies, such as the mystery of the Trinity and Unity.
claims: Gregory's 'they know all' refers to beatifying knowledge.

pl-l2d11c2.summary: Asks whether good angels advance in merit or reward until judgment. Some say they do: they serve our benefit daily and grow in knowledge and love of God, charity being both merit and reward; they grew in knowing the mystery of the Incarnation (Isa 63:1; Ps 23:8; Eph 3:10, per Jerome). Augustine seems to deny they were ignorant of it; following Haymo, the higher angels knew it in part from the ages, the lower only after its fulfillment. Others say angels after confirmation grew only in knowledge of external things, not in contemplating the Trinity or in charity, nor in merit as to its power, though in number of good deeds. Lombard finds the first view more probable, that angels advance in knowledge and other things until judgment; Isidore's and Gregory's statements that angels know all concern what beatifies, the mystery of the Trinity.
claims: One view: good angels advance in merit and reward until judgment.
The angels came to know the mystery of the Incarnation more fully after its fulfillment.
Higher angels knew the mystery partially beforehand; lower angels learned it when fulfilled (Haymo).
Another view: angels grew only in knowledge of external things, not in contemplation or charity.
Lombard finds more probable that angels advance in knowledge and other things until judgment.
Statements that angels know all refer to what beatifies, the mystery of the Trinity.
